clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa7_association_analysis: Two-sample t-test (controlling for age, sex, mean FD) for FCS patterns; comparisons of demographic and clinical variables (age, sex, educational level, Y-BOCS, illness duration, age of onset, mean FD) between subtypes. Subtype 1 patients were older and had a later age of onset compared to subtype 2.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: Two distinct neurophysiological subtypes of OCD were identified based on individualized functional connectome abnormalities, showing contrasting patterns of functional connectivity strength deviations and significant differences in age of onset.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa9_key_findings_detailed: K-means clustering identified two distinct OCD subtypes. Subtype 1 (73.74%, n=73) showed significantly decreased Functional Connectivity Strength (FCS) in regions like the frontal gyrus, insula, hippocampus, and precentral/postcentral gyrus. Subtype 2 (26.26%, n=26) exhibited increased FCS in widespread brain regions including the superior medial frontal gyrus, inferior frontal gyrus, middle frontal gyrus, thalamus, striatum, and middle occipital gyrus. No significant FCS abnormalities were observed when all OCD patients were pooled. Subtype 1 patients were slightly older (t=2.17, p=0.032) and had a later age of onset (t=2.52, p=0.014) compared to subtype 2.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa11_application_notes: Sensitivity analyses for reproducibility included 1000 iterations of k-means clustering on 90% subsamples of patients, and validation using the Automated Anatomical Labeling (AAL) atlas.

caa10_key_limitations.answer: The study used a cross-sectional sample, limiting generalizability; clinical information was limited, restricting exploration of other clinical differences; factors like BMI and alcohol/cigarette use were not controlled; OCD patients had lower educational levels than HCs.

general_note_part.gn1_general_notes: Functional connectivity strength (FCS) analysis was constrained to correlations surpassing a threshold of r = 0.2 to exclude weak correlations.
